question.prompt: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(D\) lies on \(BC\), \(BD:DC=1:2\), and \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AD\). Draw \(BE\) and extend it to intersect \(AC\) at \(F\). Find the value of \(AF/FC\). (Express the result as a fraction in lowest terms.)

solutions.explanation: Through \(D\), draw \(DG\parallel BF\), intersecting \(AC\) at \(G\). Since \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AD\) and \(EF\parallel DG\), \(AF=FG\). Also, since \(DG\parallel BF\), \(CG/GF=CD/DB=2\), giving \(GC=2FG\). Therefore, \(AF:FC=1:3\), and the value is \(1/3\).
solutions.title: Construct a parallel line

solutions.explanation:
The midpoint condition gives equal areas, which lets us carry the given ratio on \(BC\) over to \(AC\). Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of \(\triangle XYZ\). Since \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AD\), \(BE\) is a median of \(\triangle ABD\), so
\[
[ABE]=[DBE].
\]
Also, \(BC=3BD\). Triangles \(BCE\) and \(BDE\) have the same altitude from \(E\) to \(BC\), so \([BCE]=3[DBE]\). Therefore
\[
\frac{[ABE]}{[CBE]}=\frac13.
\]
The point \(E\) lies inside \(\triangle ABC\), so \(B,E,F\) occur in that order. Let \(t=BE/BF>0\). For each of the vertices \(A\) and \(C\), changing the base from \(BF\) to \(BE\) leaves the altitude to that line unchanged. Thus \([ABE]=t[ABF]\) and \([CBE]=t[CBF]\). Cancelling the positive factor \(t\) gives \([ABF]/[CBF]=1/3\).

Finally, triangles \(ABF\) and \(CBF\) share the altitude from \(B\) to \(AC\), so their area ratio equals their base ratio. Hence
\[
\frac{AF}{FC}=\frac{[ABF]}{[CBF]}=\frac13.
\]
solutions.title: Compare triangle areas
